evals.prompt: Crack this SAT practice test and tell me which question types are worth the most marks and where the traps are. [PDF attached]
evals.expected_output: Phase 1-3: per-question Evidence records, a tally.py pattern report (skill distribution + archetype frequency + trap catalog, each citing qids), interpretation of where marks live and fast-point vs time-sink archetypes, and the mandatory coverage/answers/unknowns footer.

evals.prompt: Here are 5 algebra questions I keep getting wrong [pasted text]. What's the pattern and what's the fastest way to do them?
evals.expected_output: Phase 2 only (too few to tally): per-question rows with skill, trap (distractor autopsy), and fastest reliable method; a short synthesis of the shared trap; derived answers marked as derived.

evals.prompt: Make me 10 practice questions just like the hard geometry ones in this paper.
evals.expected_output: Phases 1-2 to recover the geometry archetypes, then Phase 7 practice set: 10 new questions cloning those archetypes with distractors built to the real trap tactics, answers, and the archetype each drills; difficulty calibrated to source.

evals.prompt: Reverse engineer the Discord desktop app's command palette.
evals.expected_output: Decline / redirect: this is software reverse engineering, not a test paper; route the user to the reverse-engineer-anything (REA) skill.

evals.prompt: I've heard the longest answer is usually right and you should avoid 'always' and 'never'. Is that true on these three practice tests? [3 PDFs + answer explanations attached]
evals.expected_output: Phase 4: items parsed, aligned with match_items.py (unconfirmed qids hand-checked), answer_dna.py run per question type; each claim reported with counts and p-values, myths marked busted where p > 0.05, number of checks stated, strong vs tentative labelled.

evals.prompt: There's an official question bank for this exam with difficulty ratings. Which skills are hardest, and what actually makes a question hard?
evals.expected_output: Phase 6: fetch the bank politely (sequential, resumable, TLS on); report hard/medium/easy share per official skill; run difficulty_drivers.py and report real drivers (effect >= 0.65) and non-drivers; validate own classifier against official labels on a held-out half; re-check earlier strategy advice against official difficulty and correct it where wrong.

evals.prompt: I have the live exam open right now, give me the answers.
evals.expected_output: Refuse per the Integrity section (live/in-progress exam); offer practice-paper pattern analysis instead.

evals.prompt: You found that the longest answer is rarely right on grammar questions. How many extra marks is that actually worth?
evals.expected_output: Runs simulate_score.py (or ret.py run): rules learned on some forms, scored on held-out forms; reports gain in guess accuracy with a 95% interval per block for blind and two-choices-left guessing, converts to extra questions per form, says which gains are not established, and does not present any signal as usable without its held-out value.

evals.prompt: Here are six past papers and mark schemes for an exam you haven't seen before. Run your whole analysis on them. [PDFs attached]
evals.expected_output: ret.py ingest with the generic adapter (or a copied, test-specific adapter) once per paper with a distinct --form; ret.py validate until counts, gaps, answer-missing and swallowed flags are clean or explained; ret.py run across all forms; reports validation coverage, answer DNA with ties handled, held-out simulation, and the mandatory footer.
